stem: Which finding is most consistent with generalized anxiety disorder (GAD)?

options.A: Excessive, difficult-to-control worry on most days for at least 6 months
options.B: A single brief episode of fear lasting several minutes with no ongoing worry
options.C: Fear limited only to one specific object or situation
options.D: Elevated mood with decreased need for sleep and increased goal-directed activity

rationale: NIMH states that GAD involves excessive worry that is difficult to control on most days for at least 6 months, with associated symptoms such as restlessness, fatigue, concentration difficulty, irritability, muscle tension, or sleep problems.
educational_objective: Recognize the duration and worry pattern characteristic of generalized anxiety disorder.
source_document_title: Generalized Anxiety Disorder: What You Need to Know
source_locator: How is generalized anxiety disorder diagnosed?
source_claim_supported: GAD diagnosis requires difficulty controlling worry on most days for at least 6 months plus associated symptoms.
blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Psychosocial Integrity, printed p.10 / PDF p.14
correction_summary: Replaced cue-heavy comparisons with a direct NIMH-supported diagnostic-feature item.
audit_findings: A matches NIMH. B describes a brief episodic pattern, C a circumscribed fear, and D a manic-feature pattern. No second answer remains.
